id_paramount_rock.blurb: Paramount Rock is a hillside wall in Kelly Canyon, east of Idaho Falls and a few miles past Ririe. It holds 17 climbs, mostly sport with a handful of trad lines, plus one V4 boulder problem. Grades run from the high 5.7s into the 5.11s, with most routes in the 5.8 to 5.10 band, so it suits newer leaders as well as climbers working up the grades. The wall catches the morning sun and goes shady later in the day, which makes summer afternoons tolerable, though wind is common. Most lines are climbable on a 50 m rope. It is visible from the road, a short uphill hike from the pullout.

id_lower_breadloaves_provo_wall.blurb: Provo Wall is the southernmost crag of the Breadloaves, the upper-city zone of City of Rocks near Almo. It is the east-facing side of Decadent Wall, so it gets sun early and shade by afternoon. Seventeen climbs, split between ten trad lines and seven sport routes, cover cracks, roofs and an overhanging offwidth on granite. Difficulty starts with a 5.6 and climbs to the low 5.12s, with the bulk of routes between 5.8 and 5.11. Bolts and gear routes mix on the same face, and more anchors have been added over the years. A rappel station at the left end of the crag gives an easy way down.

id_wavewall.blurb: WaveWall is a small bouldering wall on the south side of Pocatello, tucked between a game fence and the interstate. It is the smallest of the local bouldering areas but also the nearest to town, with only a minute or so of walking from the pullout. The wall is roughly 15 to 20 feet high and 30 to 40 feet long, with flat landings, a walk-around to the base and good top-outs. Seventeen problems range from V0 up to a V12 project, with a good spread through the middle grades and a hard end for strong climbers. Many eliminates and link-ups are possible.
